rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Sequential read, chunk by chunk. Chunk1 L5 'all three of these...: access to private data, exposure to untrusted content, and a channel that communicates out' resolves in the same sentence (colon-introduced list, not a forward pointer to a later slide); 'leg'/'legs' at L6-7 read off that same-chunk list. Chunk3 is the closest calls: L17 'This asks who attacks the agent building it' -- 'This' = the frame the chunk's own header just named ('The attacker targets the agent, not the system') plus L5's 'Simon Willison's frame', both in-file antecedents; L18 'The two audits compose' -- 'the two audits' is named one clause later in the SAME sentence ('An access-surface map and a STRIDE pass'), immediate intra-bullet cataphora, not a cross-slide forward reference (the stranded-by-re-chunk test asks whether an antecedent sits buried several slides back -- this sits one comma away). Chunk4 L23-26 'the three legs'/'a leg'/'one goes' all resolve to chunk1's list -- arc-earned reuse within one file, the rule's own NOT-violation example. No pronoun or demonstrative anywhere lacks an in-file antecedent by the time it's read.

No sentence locates a claim in another file by position. Chunk3 L18 names the two other frameworks by title, unpacked in the same clause ('An access-surface map and a STRIDE pass on the feature'), which is the rule's own PASS form ('name the source by title or by its claim'), not 'the module on security said...'. Grep over body_numbered for module/lecture/prework/earlier/previous/this-training positional pointer language returns zero hits.

Every content chunk carries 3-4 full bullets with its own self-carrying claim: chunk1 (three-leg frame, structural-not-risky claim, ordinary-wiring examples), chunk2 (instruction/data inseparability, prompt injection naming), chunk3 (agent-vs-system target shift, two-audits-compose, accident-vs-adversary split), chunk4 (audit-and-cut procedure, concrete mitigations, Willison's constraint quote, filter critique, closer). None is a bare wait-state or single context-dependent bullet.

Checked each header against its own chunk's content. L3 'Three capabilities that must not meet' -> chunk names exactly three (L5) and argues they're structural not risky (L6). L9 'An LLM can't reliably tell instructions from data' -> chunk's first bullet (L11) states exactly this and elaborates. L15 'The attacker targets the agent, not the system' -> chunk contrasts classic system-threat-modeling with agent-targeting (L17). L21 'Removing any one leg breaks the trifecta' -> chunk is entirely the audit-and-cut-a-leg procedure (L23-26). No header is contradicted by its own chunk's body.

Checked each sub-item against every chunk. 'Not X. Not Y. Z.': only candidate is L6 'Not risky. Structural.' -- one negation followed by one affirmation, not the banned double-negation-then-affirmation shape; stays inside as ordinary contrastive phrasing, occurs once in the file. Anaphora/epistrophe triples: no three consecutive bullets share an opening word or clause shape; L23's 'what private data can it read, what untrusted content reaches it, what channels leave the machine' is a three-part parallel but each leg names a distinct concrete check (data/content/channel), satisfying the rule's own 'third leg carries NEW concrete content' exemption rather than tripping it. Self-grading superlatives: grep for most/best/one-of-the/useful returns zero. Number + retraction: no digits anywhere in body, nothing to retract. Abstraction-noun stacks: 'context window', 'access-surface map' are standard security-engineering compounds, not invented nominalizations. Verb triplets with an empty leg: none present. No sub-item fires.

Doesn't matter here: the maintainer block frames it as law-teaching content ('Laws carried: lethal-trifecta -- instructions-vs-data inseparability'), exactly the case the current wording generalises to ('the claim requirement binds law and consolidation slides -- where the header IS the teaching'). All four headers are full declarative claims, not labels: L3 'Three capabilities that must not meet' (a prohibition, not a bare catalogue noun like 'Ralph'), L9 'An LLM can't reliably tell instructions from data', L15 'The attacker targets the agent, not the system', L21 'Removing any one leg breaks the trifecta' -- each states a claim the chunk beneath it then argues for. rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked all three sub-classes against every bullet. (a) doctrine restatement: closest call is chunk4's last two sentences (L26) 'Detection lowers the odds; only removing a leg changes the structure. In security, cut a leg instead of trusting a filter.' -- stays inside because the second sentence converts the first's descriptive mechanism claim into an actionable directive (what to DO, not a re-announcement of what was already argued), which is the 'priority' the rule asks a surviving bullet to add. No other bullet re-announces a law already argued elsewhere; the diff since the last pin actually REMOVED one near-restatement (chunk2's bullet used to open 'An LLM cannot reliably tell instructions from data,' mirroring its own header almost verbatim -- now cut, leaving only the elaboration). (b) self-referential design commentary: zero hits, this is security content with no meta-pedagogy framing. (c) aphorism kicker: closest call is L28 'Three legs. Cut one.' -- a whole-file closer, not a mid-chunk restatement of chunk4's own header; matches rule 2's own endorsed pattern ('a closer summing the whole deck is a closer doing its job') rather than the banned in-chunk koan shape, and has stood through five prior audit stamps unchanged.
